title: Elementary coefficient comparison law predicates
statement: At the recorded finite, completed integral, rational and common-field coefficient stages, define the elementary coefficient law predicates as follows. Direct-image scalar laws assert the canonical comparison isomorphisms; support scalar laws assert their constructible isomorphisms and the actual proper/open composition equations. The mate equations are the two unit/counit equations for coefficient pullback and direct image. Tower and identity laws compare the recorded scalar associators and units, including direct and support maps. Integral-stage associator and unit are those of the coefficient transition system; integral coefficient coherence requires their equations for supplied transition isomorphisms. The direct-image coefficient action is the recorded coherent action on finite coefficient stages. The three common-stage representative predicates identify pullback, tensor and permitted internal-Hom comparisons with their finite-field representatives. Each law retains its existing constructibility, invertibility, geometry and representative hypotheses; no theorem establishing these laws is included. The constituent notions are [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] [def-weil-derived-direct-image] [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] [def-pur-operation-scalar-transport].
